title: The 14-Day Rotation

background.schedule: 2 meals on most days; restaurant breakfast on weekends; Wednesdays are protein-shake days

tuna.title: Spicy tuna–avocado rice bowl
ingredients: 2 cans light tuna (170 g each before draining); drain both
steps: If rice is not already cooked, cook it in your rice cooker following its manual; allow additional time. Measure 1½ cups after cooking. Reheat refrigerated rice until thoroughly hot.
Drain both tuna cans. Dice half a cucumber and half an avocado.
Mix 1 tsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp lime juice and optional ½ tsp sriracha in a bowl.
Flake the drained tuna into the sauce with a fork and mix for 20 seconds.
Put the hot rice in a bowl and top with tuna, avocado and cucumber. Serve.
tuna.tip: Canned tuna is already cooked. Sriracha is optional.
tuna.before: Rice must be cooked first (use rice cooker if needed). Tuna is canned and ready to eat.

gingerbeef.title: Sticky ginger beef noodles
ingredients: 90 g DRY Blue Dragon SOBA (about 1 of the 3 tied bundles in the 250 g pack; NOT the whole package)
steps: Mince one garlic clove and grate 1 tsp fresh ginger. Keep the broccoli frozen; it goes straight into the skillet.
Mix soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and 2 tbsp water in a small bowl.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 225 g ground beef and break it apart for 5–7 minutes, until fully cooked to 71°C / 160°F. Drain excess fat if needed.
Add 2 cups frozen broccoli and 2 tbsp water to the beef. Cover over medium heat for 4–6 minutes, stirring halfway, until thoroughly hot.

Meanwhile boil a pot of water. Remove just ONE bundle (~83 g) of the THREE tied bundles from the 250 g pack, or use a scale to weigh exactly 90 g dry. Keep remaining bundles dry. Add this SOBA portion; Blue Dragon's package says 3 minutes (follow your own package if different). Drain immediately. Do not use penne cooking times.
Pour the sauce over beef and broccoli. Stir 1 minute over medium heat; add drained soba, toss for 30 seconds and serve.
gingerbeef.tip: Soba for ginger beef; penne for meatball marinara. The complete 250 g soba package has three tied bundles, about 83 g each. Use only one bundle for one serving. Your soba package indicates 3 minutes.
gingerbeef.before: WARNING: the 250 g Blue Dragon soba pack contains THREE tied bundles. For one serving, use just ONE bundle (about 83 g dry), close to the listed 90 g, or weigh precisely 90 g dry. Do NOT cook the whole 250 g package. Frozen broccoli does not need thawing.

lemonpotato.title: Lemony chicken and potato bowl
ingredients: 225 g ALREADY COOKED chicken breast or thigh
300 g REGULAR potatoes from the 2.27 kg bag, cut into 2 cm cubes
Pinch of salt and black pepper
steps: Confirm chicken is ALREADY COOKED. If raw, cut into strips and pan-cook on medium-high for 6–10 minutes, until 74°C / 165°F; allow extra time.
Weigh 300 g regular potatoes from the grocery bag. Wash; peeling is optional. Cut into approximately 2 cm cubes (do not simply halve).

Put cubes in a microwave-safe dish with 2 tbsp water. Cover loosely to vent steam. Microwave on high for 7–10 minutes, stirring halfway. Test with a fork; if still firm, continue in 1-minute intervals.
Dice ½ cup tomatoes and ½ cup cucumber. Cut cooked chicken into 2 cm bites.
Whisk together 2 tsp olive oil, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tbsp lemon juice, ¼ tsp oregano and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Reheat pre-cooked chicken until hot, then mix with potatoes and vegetables. Toss in dressing and serve.
lemonpotato.tip: The same REGULAR-potato bag covers lemon chicken, salmon, chili potato and tuna-potato salad. Microwave time depends on cube size and appliance.
lemonpotato.before: Use REGULAR potatoes from the 2.27 kg bag, not baby potatoes. Weigh 300 g and dice into 2 cm cubes for even microwave cooking. Chicken must ALREADY BE COOKED, otherwise cook it separately.

fajitas.title: Smoky chicken fajita rice bowls
ingredients: 2 bell peppers, seeded and cut into strips
2 cups (500 mL) ALREADY COOKED rice, for both portions
steps: Cook rice in your rice cooker first if necessary, following its manual. You need 2 cups AFTER cooking for the two servings.
Cut 450 g raw chicken into 1–2 cm strips; slice peppers and onion. Use a separate cutting surface for raw poultry.
Season chicken with 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp cumin, salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high for 1 minute; add 1 tbsp olive oil and chicken. Stir-cook 5–8 minutes until the thickest strip reaches 74°C / 165°F.
Add peppers and onion; stir-cook another 5–7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Divide the chicken-vegetable mixture equally. Eat one half with 1 cup cooked rice, 1 tbsp salsa and lime.
Promptly refrigerate the other half of the chicken-vegetable mixture in a covered container for Thursday lunch. Have another cup of cooked rice ready for Thursday.
fajitas.tip: Makes two chicken-and-vegetable servings: one Tuesday, one Thursday. Chill leftovers promptly.
fajitas.before: Cook rice first; make TWO chicken/pepper servings and refrigerate one for Thursday.

fajitaleft.title: Fajita black-bean bowl
ingredients: 1 refrigerated serving of ALREADY COOKED chicken and peppers from Tuesday
¾ cup (180 mL) canned black beans, rinsed and drained
½ cup (125 mL) frozen corn kernels
steps: Take Tuesday's cooked chicken and peppers from the refrigerator. Only use it if it was chilled promptly and kept refrigerated.
Drain and rinse black beans; measure ¾ cup. Measure ½ cup corn straight from the freezer.
Put chicken, peppers, 1 cup cooked rice, beans, corn and 2 tbsp water into a skillet over medium heat. Cover 5–7 minutes, stirring twice, until leftovers are piping hot (74°C / 165°F).
Transfer to a bowl. Top with 1 tbsp salsa and 1 tsp lime juice, then serve.
fajitaleft.tip: This is a LEFTOVER chicken recipe; do not use raw chicken. Refrigerate cooked rice promptly.
fajitaleft.before: Uses already-cooked Tuesday fajita chicken plus cooked rice.

salmon.title: Maple–Dijon salmon with potatoes
ingredients: 225 g RAW salmon fillet, thawed if previously frozen
300 g REGULAR potatoes from the 2.27 kg bag (raw weight; do not buy baby potatoes)
2 cups (500 mL) FROZEN cut green beans
2 tbsp (30 mL) water for the green beans
steps: If salmon is frozen, thaw in the refrigerator, preferably overnight. Preheat the oven to 200°C / 400°F and wait until it is fully heated. Prepare a large baking sheet; line with parchment if available.

Weigh 300 g REGULAR RAW potatoes from the 2.27 kg grocery bag. Rinse and scrub; trim any bad spots. Leave the skins on if you like. Cut into evenly sized 2 cm cubes: first 2 cm slices, then sticks, then cubes. Do not simply halve them—these are not baby potatoes.
Spread the cubes in ONE even layer on the tray, without piling up. Add 2 tsp olive oil, ¼ tsp black pepper and optional pinch of salt; toss with clean hands or a spatula to coat all sides.

Place the tray in the HOT oven and set a timer for 15 minutes. At 15 minutes, remove the tray and turn the cubes with a spatula. Return to the oven for another 10–20 minutes (25–35 minutes total). They are ready when lightly golden outside and a fork easily passes through the centre of a cube.
While the potatoes roast, stir together 1 tbsp Dijon and 2 tsp maple syrup. Pat the salmon dry with paper towel (do not rinse), put on a separate small tray and spread the glaze evenly on top.

AFTER the potatoes have roasted for 15 minutes and have been turned, put the salmon tray on another rack or alongside. Bake about 10–15 minutes according to thickness. Check the thickest part with a thermometer: aim for 70°C / 158°F. If salmon is ready before the potatoes, remove it, tent loosely and finish roasting potatoes.

With about 8 minutes remaining, put 2 cups still-FROZEN green beans in a small saucepan with 2 tbsp water. Cover and heat on medium for about 6–8 minutes, stirring halfway, until hot and tender. Drain leftover water; do not thaw first.
Plate the 300 g roast potatoes, salmon and green beans; drizzle 1 tbsp lemon juice over fish and vegetables. Serve immediately.
salmon.tip: Use the REGULAR potatoes already purchased in the 2.27 kg bag; no extra grocery purchase. Larger-than-2-cm cubes will take longer, so use the fork test. Potatoes roast 25–35 minutes total; salmon goes in after the first 15 minutes. For a smaller plate, use 200 g potatoes; nutrition estimates will change.
salmon.before: Use REGULAR potatoes from the 2.27 kg grocery bag, NOT baby potatoes. Weigh 300 g RAW and cut into evenly sized 2 cm cubes; do not just halve them. No peeling or pre-boiling required. If salmon is frozen, thaw safely in the refrigerator before cooking.

meatballs.title: Garlicky meatball marinara pasta
ingredients: 150 g Compliments Angus beef FROZEN FULLY COOKED meatballs (680 g bag; keep remaining 530 g frozen)
90 g dry PENNE RIGATE pasta (not soba)
2 tbsp (30 mL) water if sauce is too thick
steps: Confirm the frozen meatballs are FULLY COOKED. If so, no thawing is required; if RAW, cook fully according to package before continuing.
Mince one garlic clove. Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; stir garlic for 30 seconds without browning.
Add ¾ cup marinara and 2 tbsp water if thick. Add 150 g frozen fully cooked meatballs; cover.
Simmer over medium-low 15–20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until meatballs are hot in the centre (74°C / 165°F for reheating). Follow package directions if different.
Meanwhile boil a pot of water. Add 90 g dry PENNE (not soba); cook for the time listed on your PENNE package and drain.
Add 2 cups spinach, 1 tsp dried basil and optional ¼ tsp pepper flakes to hot meatballs. Stir-cook 1–2 minutes until wilted.
Toss drained penne into sauce for 30 seconds and serve.
meatballs.tip: This recipe uses PENNE RIGATE, NOT soba. Correction to the earlier meal: if you cooked the ENTIRE 250 g dry soba pack with meatballs and ate half of the cooked noodles, that equals about 125 g dry noodles eaten, NOT 45 g. Long Phung 216 g beef balls are springy Vietnamese-style, unlike Italian meatballs.
meatballs.before: For the NEXT order use Compliments regular Angus beef meatballs, 680 g bag (use 150 g), with no cheese listed in the published ingredients. Do NOT buy Long Phung 216 g Vietnamese meatballs for marinara; they are springy. Already-bought Long Phung can be eaten but will remain firm.

chili.title: Smoky turkey and black-bean chili
ingredients: 600 g RAW lean ground turkey (two packs if each is 450 g)
1 can (540 mL) black beans, rinsed and drained
1 medium onion, peeled and diced (about 1 cup)
steps: Check turkey pack weight: recipe uses 600 g RAW. A single 450 g pack also works but yields less meat/protein in each portion.
Dice onion and bell pepper. Drain and rinse the black beans.
Heat a large pot over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp oil, onion and pepper; stir 4–5 minutes until softening.
Add raw turkey; break up and stir for 6–8 minutes until fully cooked to 74°C / 165°F.
Stir in the entire can of crushed tomatoes, drained beans, 2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika and ¼ tsp salt.
Reduce to medium-low; simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring every 4–5 minutes. If too thick, add 2–4 tbsp water.
Divide into roughly 3 portions. Eat one on Friday, chill the others promptly in shallow containers and FREEZE at least one for Week 2 Monday's chili potato.
chili.tip: Three portions total; save and freeze at least one for next week's loaded potato.
chili.before: 600 g RAW ground turkey (two 450 g packs if needed); save one portion for Week 2.

porkchop.title: Garlic–lime pork chops and sweet potato
ingredients: 225–250 g RAW boneless lean pork chop
350 g sweet potato, washed and cut into 1–2 cm thick wedges
2 cups (500 mL) bagged shredded cabbage slaw
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C / 400°F. Cut sweet potato into 1–2 cm thick wedges, spread on a tray and toss with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt.
Roast 20–30 minutes, turning after 12–15 minutes, until fork-tender.
Mince 1 garlic clove; season both sides of the pork chop with garlic, ½ tsp paprika, salt and pepper.
Heat a skillet over medium-high with remaining 1 tsp oil. Cook chop about 4–6 minutes per side depending on thickness; check 71°C / 160°F in the centre. Rest 3 minutes.
Mix 2 cups shredded cabbage with 1 tbsp vinegar and 1 tbsp lime juice for about 20 seconds.
Serve pork, sweet potato and slaw together.
porkchop.tip: Use a thermometer for the pork; the time depends on chop thickness.
porkchop.before: Raw boneless pork chop and raw sweet potato. Oven and skillet are used separately.

thaicurry.title: Thai red shrimp curry
ingredients: 250 g RAW peeled, deveined, THAWED shrimp
2 cups (500 mL) frozen Asian-style stir-fry vegetable blend
1 tbsp (15 mL) Thai red curry paste; add more only after tasting
1½ cups (375 mL) ALREADY COOKED jasmine rice
steps: If shrimp are frozen, thaw overnight in the refrigerator or in a sealed bag in cold water, changing the water every 30 minutes. Drain; never thaw on the counter.
Cook jasmine rice in your rice cooker if needed, following its instructions. Measure 1½ cups AFTER cooking.
Heat a skillet or saucepan over medium. Stir in 1 tbsp red curry paste for 30 seconds without burning.
Pour in 1 cup coconut milk and add 2 cups frozen Asian vegetables directly from the freezer. Cover and simmer over medium-low for 6–8 minutes until hot.

Add 250 g raw thawed shrimp; simmer for about 3–5 minutes depending on size, stirring until opaque, firm and 74°C / 165°F in the centre. If shrimp are PRECOOKED, add only at the end for 1–2 minutes to reheat.
Stir in 1 tbsp lime juice, taste, and add extra curry paste only if desired. Spoon over 1½ cups cooked rice; optional cilantro on top.
thaicurry.tip: Add frozen vegetables straight to the sauce. Thaw raw shrimp first. If using pre-cooked shrimp, only reheat at the end.
thaicurry.before: Thaw RAW shrimp ahead of time; use already-cooked rice and frozen vegetables.

chilipotato.title: Chili-loaded baked potato
ingredients: 1 portion (about ⅓ of the batch) of COOKED Friday turkey chili, frozen for this meal
steps: Move a frozen portion of Friday's chili to the fridge the night before to thaw. If still frozen, microwave on defrost and reheat immediately.
Wash the 350 g russet potato and pierce 5–6 times with a fork. Put it on a microwave-safe plate.
Microwave on high approximately 7–10 minutes, turning halfway, until a fork slides through its centre. Rest 1 minute.
Microwave thawed chili in a covered microwave-safe bowl for 2–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until uniformly hot to 74°C / 165°F.
Dice 2 tbsp onion. Split potato lengthwise, spoon chili over it, top with onion and optional hot sauce and green onion.
chilipotato.tip: Uses a portion of cooked chili saved from Week 1. Do NOT start a new batch of chili.
chilipotato.before: Thaw a cooked portion of chili from Week 1 in the refrigerator the night before.

oregano.title: Lemon–oregano chicken rice bowl
ingredients: 225 g RAW boneless chicken breast or thigh
1 lemon for 1 tbsp juice and a little zest
steps: Cook rice in the rice cooker first if needed, following its manual. Measure 1½ cups AFTER cooking.
Wash lemon, grate about ¼ tsp zest, then squeeze 1 tbsp juice. Mince one garlic clove. Cut 225 g raw chicken into even ~2 cm pieces.
Coat chicken in garlic, lemon zest, ½ tsp oregano, salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken 6–10 minutes, turning regularly, until every piece reaches 74°C / 165°F.
Dice ¾ cup tomatoes and ¾ cup cucumber; toss with 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Put hot cooked rice in a bowl; add cooked chicken and tomato-cucumber salad.
oregano.tip: Substitute ½ tsp dried basil if you have no dried oregano.
oregano.before: Use RAW chicken and rice measured AFTER cooking.

peanutnoodle.title: Thai peanut chicken noodles
ingredients: 90 g dry FLAT RICE noodles for Pad Thai (not soba or penne)
1 tsp (5 mL) sweet chili sauce or hot sauce, to taste
steps: Identify the right noodles: use FLAT RICE NOODLES for Pad Thai. Read THEIR package for soaking or boiling directions; do not use soba or penne timing.
Cut raw chicken into 1–2 cm strips; measure 1 cup shredded cabbage and 1 cup shredded carrots. Leave vegetables raw for crunch.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, 1 tsp chili sauce and 2 tbsp hot water in a bowl. Add another tbsp water if too thick.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-high. Add chicken and 2 tbsp water to prevent sticking; cook 6–10 minutes, stirring, until chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F.
While chicken cooks, prepare 90 g flat rice noodles according to their own package; drain as soon as tender.
Turn skillet to low. Toss chicken, cooked noodles, peanut sauce, cabbage and carrots for 1–2 minutes until hot; serve.
peanutnoodle.tip: SOBA = ginger beef; PENNE = meatballs; FLAT RICE NOODLES = peanut chicken. Each has separate cooking directions.
peanutnoodle.before: Use FLAT RICE NOODLES, not soba or penne; follow their package.

tacoskillet.title: Smoky taco beef skillet
ingredients: ¾ cup (180 mL) canned black beans, rinsed and drained
½ cup (125 mL) frozen corn kernels
steps: If rice isn't ready, cook it in your rice cooker per its manual; measure 1 cup AFTER cooking.
Dice half a bell pepper. Rinse and drain ¾ cup black beans and measure ½ cup still-frozen corn.
Heat a skillet over medium-high and brown 225 g raw beef, breaking it up for 5–7 minutes until fully cooked to 71°C / 160°F. Drain excess fat.
Add diced pepper and spices (½ tsp chili powder, ¼ tsp each cumin and smoked paprika); stir over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add beans, frozen corn and 2 tbsp water. Cover over medium heat for 3–5 minutes until corn is hot, stirring once.
Add the hot mixture to 1 cup cooked rice in a bowl; top with 2 tbsp salsa and diced ⅓ avocado.
tacoskillet.tip: Keep corn frozen until adding directly to the pan. Canned beans are pre-cooked.
tacoskillet.before: Use RAW ground beef and already-cooked rice; corn goes in frozen.

shrimpmango.title: Chili–lime shrimp mango bowl
ingredients: 250 g RAW peeled, deveined, THAWED shrimp
¼ tsp crushed red pepper flakes (optional)
steps: Thaw raw frozen shrimp overnight in the fridge or in a closed bag in cold water (change water every 30 minutes). Drain and pat dry.
Cook rice in the rice cooker if necessary following its manual. Measure 1½ cups AFTER cooking.
Peel and dice half the mango; dice half the cucumber. Toss together with 1 tbsp lime juice and optional pepper flakes.
Heat 2 tsp olive oil over medium-high in a skillet. Add 250 g thawed raw shrimp in one layer. Cook about 2–3 minutes per side until opaque and firm, checking 74°C / 165°F in the centre.
Serve shrimp and mango-cucumber mix over hot rice. Add optional chopped cilantro.
shrimpmango.tip: If using PRECOOKED shrimp, heat them only 1–2 minutes instead of cooking again.
shrimpmango.before: Thaw RAW shrimp in the refrigerator ahead of time; use already-cooked rice.

harissa.title: Harissa chicken and chickpea tray bake
ingredients: 225 g RAW chicken, cut into 2 cm cubes
¾ cup (180 mL) canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Preheat oven to 205°C / 400°F. Optionally line a baking sheet with parchment.
Drain and rinse ¾ cup chickpeas. Slice one pepper and half an onion; use a separate cutting surface to cube raw chicken into 2 cm pieces.
Mix 1 tbsp harissa paste and 2 tsp olive oil in a bowl. Add chicken, chickpeas and vegetables; toss to coat.
Spread out on the tray without crowding. Roast at 205°C for 15 minutes, then turn pieces with a spatula.
Roast another 5–10 minutes until chicken is cooked through to 74°C / 165°F and vegetables are tender.
Squeeze half a lemon over the tray and serve. If harissa is very hot, use only ½ tbsp.
harissa.tip: Canned chickpeas are already cooked; roasting crisps them. Check the chicken's internal temperature.
harissa.before: Uses RAW chicken and canned, already-cooked chickpeas.

tunabeans.title: Tuna, white bean and potato salad
ingredients: 2 cans light tuna (170 g each before draining), drained
¾ cup (180 mL) canned white beans, rinsed and drained
250 g REGULAR potatoes from the 2.27 kg bag, diced into 2 cm cubes
½ finely minced garlic clove (about ½ tsp)
steps: Weigh 250 g regular potatoes, wash and dice into even 2 cm cubes without needing to peel. Put cubes in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp water; cover loosely to vent steam.
Microwave on high for 6–9 minutes, stirring halfway, until easily pierced with a fork. Add 1-minute increments if needed; cool 2 minutes.
Meanwhile drain both tuna cans. Rinse and drain white beans; measure ¾ cup.
Wash and halve enough cherry tomatoes for 1 cup. Mince ½ garlic clove and chop 1 tbsp fresh parsley.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic and black pepper in a small bowl.
Mix warm potatoes, white beans, tomatoes, tuna and parsley; toss gently with dressing and serve.
tunabeans.tip: Uses regular potatoes already on the grocery list, not baby potatoes. No other kind needs buying.
tunabeans.before: Use 250 g REGULAR potatoes from the same 2.27 kg bag; wash and dice into 2 cm cubes. No need for baby potatoes. Canned tuna and white beans are already cooked.

koreanbeef.title: Korean-style sticky beef bowl
ingredients: 1 tsp (5 mL) honey or maple syrup instead of brown sugar
steps: Cook rice with your rice cooker if necessary; measure 1½ cups AFTER cooking.
Cut beef into thin strips if needed. Slice mushrooms, mince garlic and grate 1 tsp ginger.
Mix soy sauce, 1 tsp honey or maple syrup, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and optional pepper flakes in a bowl.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high. Sear beef strips, stirring 3–5 minutes until fully cooked (71°C / 160°F). Move beef onto a clean plate.
Add frozen broccoli, fresh mushrooms and 2 tbsp water to skillet. Cover over medium heat 4–6 minutes, stirring, until vegetables are hot and tender.
Return beef, pour in sauce and toss for 1–2 minutes over medium heat. Serve on hot rice.
koreanbeef.tip: Use honey or maple syrup rather than buying brown sugar just for this dish.
koreanbeef.before: RAW beef strips and already-cooked rice; broccoli goes in frozen.

tomatocurry.title: Tomato–coconut chicken curry
ingredients: 250 g RAW chicken, cut into 2 cm cubes
¾ cup (180 mL) canned crushed tomatoes
½ cup (125 mL) light coconut milk
1½ cups (375 mL) ALREADY COOKED basmati rice
steps: If necessary, cook basmati rice in your rice cooker per its manual; measure 1½ cups AFTER cooking.
Dice 250 g raw chicken into ~2 cm cubes on a poultry cutting board; mince garlic and grate 1 tsp ginger.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-high; stir-cook chicken for 3–4 minutes until lightly browned outside (it is not yet fully cooked).
Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 tsp curry powder, ½ tsp garam masala, minced garlic and ginger; stir 30 seconds.
Add ¾ cup crushed tomatoes and ½ cup light coconut milk. Add 2 tbsp water if too thick. Cover and simmer over medium-low 8–12 minutes, stirring, until chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F in the centre.
Stir in 2 cups spinach for 1–2 minutes until wilted; serve over hot rice.
tomatocurry.tip: Rice quantities are AFTER cooking. Previously opened coconut milk and tomatoes must have been safely refrigerated or frozen.
tomatocurry.before: RAW chicken and already-cooked basmati rice; cook rice beforehand if necessary.

stickypork.title: Sticky sesame pork udon
ingredients: 200 g plain READY-TO-USE UDON noodles (not soba or penne)
2 cups (500 mL) frozen Asian-style stir-fry vegetables
steps: Use the correct 200 g READY-TO-USE UDON pack, NOT 3-minute soba. Check whether the specific udon package says to rinse, warm, or briefly boil.
Mince a garlic clove. Mix soy sauce, sweet chili sauce, sesame oil and 2 tbsp water in a small bowl.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high. Add 225 g raw pork strips; stir-cook 5–8 minutes until pork reaches 71°C / 160°F in the centre.
Add frozen Asian vegetables directly from freezer and minced garlic; cover and cook over medium heat 5–7 minutes, stirring halfway, until hot.
Add the 200 g prepared udon and sauce. Toss over medium heat 1–2 minutes until noodles and pork are uniformly hot.
Serve with 1 tsp sesame seeds sprinkled on top.
stickypork.tip: Soba = ginger beef; flat rice noodles = peanut chicken; udon = pork. Penne = meatball marinara.
stickypork.before: Use READY-TO-USE UDON (200 g), not soba, penne or flat rice noodles.

restaurant.title: Your regular restaurant breakfast
steps: This is your regular Saturday/Sunday breakfast AT A RESTAURANT. No home cooking or grocery shopping is required for this meal.
Order 2 eggs, 2 sausages, 2 slices rye bread and your usual portion of breakfast potatoes.
For planning only, the 850–1,100 kcal estimate is approximate; serving sizes and cooking methods vary by restaurant.
restaurant.tip: Restaurant meal: do not add any of these ingredients to the home grocery order.
restaurant.before: Restaurant meal. No home cooking or grocery purchase required.

shakechoc.title: Chocolate–banana shake (make 3)
ingredients: PER SHAKE (make three separately during the day): 1½ scoops whey, preferably chocolate
1 tsp (5 mL) unsweetened cocoa (optional with chocolate whey)
steps: These quantities make ONE shake. Repeat three times on Wednesday; full-day amount is 4½ scoops whey, 90 g oats, 3 tbsp peanut butter and 1½ bananas.
Blend 300 mL cold water and 30 g dry rolled oats for 15–20 seconds to break up the oats.
Add 1½ scoops whey, 1 tbsp peanut butter, ½ banana, optional 1 tsp cocoa and optional ice.
Blend with lid closed 30–45 seconds until smooth. If too thick, add 50 mL water and blend 10 seconds more.
Drink now, then prepare the other shakes separately later, to reach three total. Don't leave a mixed shake at room temperature for hours.
shakechoc.tip: Vanilla whey works too: use 1 tsp cocoa for a chocolate taste. Actual macros depend on scoop weight and whey brand.
shakechoc.before: Each ingredient amount is for ONE shake. Repeat THREE times on Wednesday.

shakeberry.title: Vanilla–berry shake (make 3)
ingredients: PER SHAKE (make three separately): 1½ scoops whey, preferably vanilla
100 g frozen mixed berries (straight from freezer)
steps: These quantities make ONE shake. Repeat three times on Wednesday; full-day amount is 4½ scoops whey, 90 g oats, 3 tbsp peanut butter and 300 g frozen berries.
Blend 300 mL cold water and 30 g dry oats for 15–20 seconds.
Add 1½ scoops whey, 1 tbsp peanut butter, 100 g still-frozen berries and optional ¼ tsp cinnamon. Add ice if desired.
Blend with lid closed for 45–60 seconds. If large fruit pieces remain, stop the blender, stir with a spoon, then blend another 15 seconds.
If too thick, add 50 mL water and blend 10 more seconds. Drink promptly; make the remaining shakes as needed.
shakeberry.tip: Use peanut butter, not almond butter; no extra purchase is needed. Berries go in frozen; cinnamon is optional.
shakeberry.before: Each ingredient amount is for ONE shake. Repeat THREE times on Wednesday.

notes: Nutrition figures are planning estimates, not measured values. Use ingredient labels and adjust portions to match targets.
On regular days add a protein-rich snack and optional 150–200 kcal dessert. Add a second shake or larger protein portion if needed.
Restaurant breakfast has substantial uncertainty; no fixed meal calories are promised.
Wednesday shakes are not nutritionally complete. Supplements do not make a low-variety liquid diet equivalent to balanced meals.
Cook chicken to 74°C/165°F; refrigerate leftovers promptly.
Morning supplements contribute some calories, especially collagen and fibre powder; check product labels.

Per-meal calories and protein, carbohydrate, and fat are rough estimates from common food composition values and typical package labels; brand, raw/cooked weight, sauce and oil can change the result substantially.
Rice and quinoa are stocked pantry items; rice portions in recipes refer to the cooked weight/volume, not dry rice or microwave pouches.
Voilà product links point to an example brand and size; check quantities and availability in your delivery area before ordering.
The optimized 14-day shopping view lists shelf-stable and frozen items only once. Buy fresh produce and fresh meat by week, and freeze unused portions promptly. Quantities are estimates.

shopping_note: Rice and quinoa are already in your pantry. Use your rice cooker for any recipe calling for cooked rice. Reheat refrigerated rice thoroughly; refrigerate promptly after cooking.

hints.groundbeef: 1 × 454 g package covers the 225 g meals in Weeks 1 and 2. Freeze half for Week 2.
hints.groundturkey: Chili needs 600 g RAW turkey. Voilà product comes in 450 g packs: BUY TWO, use 600 g and freeze 300 g.
hints.shrimp: Two 250 g RAW shrimp recipes = 500 g total. The Voilà product is a 340 g bag: BUY TWO, thaw only the portions you need.
hints.tuna: Each tuna recipe uses two 170 g cans: BUY FOUR cans over 14 days.
hints.whey: 9 scoops in total for six shakes across both Wednesdays; check how much you already have.
hints.onion: One 1.36 kg bag should cover both weeks; store cool and dry.
hints.broccoli: One 500 g bag should cover the two broccoli meals; check actual bag weight versus cup portions.
hints.greenbeans: One 750 g bag for the salmon meal; keep leftovers frozen.
hints.potatoes: ONE 2.27 kg bag of REGULAR potatoes covers 14 days. W1: 300 g lemon chicken + 300 g salmon (cut 2 cm cubes). W2: 350 g chili potato + 250 g tuna salad. Total 1.2 kg. NO baby potatoes needed.
hints.stirfryveg: Voilà product is a 500 g bag. Plan on two bags for the two recipes (one each week).
hints.oats: 180 g total for six shakes. One 1 kg bag lasts several rotations.
hints.blackbeans: About 2 × 540 mL cans across chili and the two bean bowls. Freeze the Week 2 portion after opening.
hints.crushedtomatoes: Week 1 needs 796 mL; Week 2 needs about ¾ cup. Buy a smaller second can if available, or freeze the extra from a second large can.
hints.corn: Only 1 cup total across both weeks; one 750 g bag lasts multiple rotations.
hints.coconutmilk: One 400 mL can is roughly enough for both curries (1½ cups total); freeze the Week 2 portion promptly.
hints.peanutbutter: Also works for Week 2's shakes; no need to buy almond butter.
hints.berries: Week 2 needs about 300 g for three berry shakes; one 600 g bag is more than enough.
hints.pasta: One 410 g penne package; the recipe needs 90 g.
hints.noodles: The 250 g pack has THREE tied bundles (~83 g each). For one ginger-beef meal, cook ONE bundle, keep the other two dry. Do NOT cook all 250 g. Penne are for meatballs.
hints.ricenoodles: One 300 g rice-noodle package; the recipe needs 90 g.
hints.udon: One 200 g package for the Week 2 pork dish.
hints.redpepperflakes: About ¼ tsp for meatball pasta; a small bag lasts several rotations.
hints.driedbasil: About 1 tsp for meatball pasta; a small bag lasts several rotations.
hints.oregano: For lemon chicken and chicken-potato bowl. If absent, dried basil or an Italian herb blend works.
hints.cocoa: For Week 1 chocolate-banana shakes; optional if your whey is already chocolate-flavored.
hints.cinnamon: Only for Week 2 berry shakes; omit if you don't have any.
hints.salt: For seasoning to taste; only buy if you're out.
hints.blackpepper: For seasoning to taste; only buy if you're out.
hints.meatballsangus: Exact product: one 680 g bag; use 150 g for penne and keep the rest frozen. NOT Long Phung (216 g, deliberately springy texture). Regular version has 14 g fat per 60 g and no listed cheese; tenderness is subjective.
